ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There is a transition-state structure in the figure, and the curved arrows need to be ignored. The R at the lower left is connected to an alkyne-bond skeleton, and the right side of the alkyne bond is connected to a chiral carbon; the right side of this chiral carbon is connected to R1, and upward it is connected through a solid wedge bond to an oxygen atom. The oxygen is further connected to a negatively charged aluminum center; aluminum is also connected to H and two R groups. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, replace the lower-left R, the right-side R1, and the two R groups on aluminum all with wildcard *. Choose a SMILES path starting from the lower-left wildcard through the alkyne bond to the chiral carbon, giving *C#C[C@@H](*), where (*) represents R1, and [C@@H] represents the chiral carbon determined by the wedge bond to oxygen in the figure. Continue from this chiral carbon through oxygen to connect to the negatively charged aluminum hydride center, and write the two R groups on aluminum as wildcard branches, giving O[AlH-](*)*. After combining, it is *C#C[C@@H](*)O[AlH-](*)*.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: Ignore all curved arrows and transcribe only the atom-bond framework. Replace the lower-left R, the right-side R1, and the two R groups on Al by `*`. Choose a SMILES path from the lower-left wildcard through the alkyne to the stereocenter: `*C#C[C@@H](*)...`, where the branch `(*)` represents R1 and `[C@@H]` records the chiral carbon shown by the wedge bond to oxygen. Continue from that stereocenter through oxygen to the negatively charged aluminum hydride, adding the two Al-bound R substituents as wildcard branches: `O[AlH-](*)*`. Combining the pieces gives `*C#C[C@@H](*)O[AlH-](*)*`.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中有一个过渡态结构，曲箭头需要忽略。左下方的 R 连接到一段炔键骨架，炔键右侧连接到一个手性碳；该手性碳右侧连有 R1，向上通过实楔键连接到氧原子。氧再连接到带负电荷的铝中心；铝上还连有 H 和两个 R 基团。推理：按题意把左下方 R、右侧 R1、以及铝上的两个 R 都替换为通配符 *。选择从左下通配符开始经过炔键到手性碳的 SMILES 路径，得到 *C#C[C@@H](*)，其中 (*) 表示 R1，且 [C@@H] 表示图中由楔形键到氧确定的手性碳。继续从该手性碳经氧连接到带负电荷的铝氢中心，并把铝上的两个 R 写成通配符分支，得到 O[AlH-](*)*。合并后为 *C#C[C@@H](*)O[AlH-](*)*。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct structure-to-SMILES route: it reads the drawn connectivity and stereochemical bond depiction, replaces all R groups with wildcard atoms, and writes one explicit SMILES. No alternative independent route is apparent because the task is simply transcription of a single chemical drawing.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the chemical drawing: an alkynyl fragment at lower left is bonded to a stereogenic carbon bearing H implicitly, R1 to the right, and O above via a bold wedge; the O is bonded to an anionic aluminum center. The aluminum is also bonded to H and two R substituents, and curved arrows in the transition-state picture are to be ignored.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt instruction that the desired output is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure and that arrows should be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions: generic R/R1 substituents can be encoded as wildcard `*`; a C≡C bond is `C#C`; tetrahedral stereochemistry at the carbon is encoded with `[C@@H]` according to the drawn wedge orientation; oxygen attached to an anionic aluminum hydride with two wildcard substituents is `O[AlH-](*)*`. Branch substituents from the stereocenter and aluminum are written in parentheses.
